title: The ring, ii
logline: Saturday. The ring drawn correctly. It took a week. The strip does it in one panel and moves on.

panels.composition: The beach, March, a cold clear day. CHLOE and WOOD walking. BARNABY carried. Her hand, in a glove.

image.prompt: a woman in a gray coat and gloves and a thin man carrying an old dog walking a cold clear March beach, clean ink with a pale wash

panels.composition: She takes the glove off to touch the dog's head. The ring. Drawn correctly: a plain band, a small stone. Exactly the size it is.

characters.pose: glove off, hand on the dog

image.prompt: close-up of a woman's bare hand resting on an old dog's head, a plain ring with a small stone drawn at its true size, clean line
image.notes: The ring, finally, correct. One panel.

panels.composition: Wood, looking at it. Then at the water.

balloons.text: July. The islands. You'll get a card. Come.

image.prompt: a thin man looking away at the water while speaking to a woman beside him on a beach

panels.composition: From behind. The three of them at the drift log. She sits on it. He doesn't. The dog between, on the sand.

image.prompt: a woman sitting on a bleached drift log and a thin man standing beside it seen from behind, an old dog on the sand between them, facing the water, clean ink with pale wash, no words

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: The ring, drawn right. 'I'll get a card.' The drift log.
